audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir/Skill/Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir while the packet chart reads Skill/Graves/Graves/Skill/Graves/Vladimir/Vladimir. The prose sides with the packet in every disputed row — whys[1] ends 'Graves owns it', whys[2] ends "Graves's peak", whys[4] says the level-6 all-in is 'genuinely Graves-favoured'. Difficulty is also mislabelled: 35.71% is not an even matchup.
audit.why: This is the one lane where Graves has three specific, findable kill windows before he is outscaled. The chart was erasing all three and then rating the lane even, which tells the player to keep fighting exactly when he should be farming.
audit.corrected: win[1], win[2], win[4] and the matching phases sides set to Graves; diffRating raised to 7/10 and the difficulty lines rewritten.

audit.why: Spike placement is right and the mechanism behind it checks out: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 falling to 16s at rank 5, so the early window really does exist before he can afford a W point, and Crimson Pact converting bonus health into AP is why his item spikes hit so hard.
audit.corrected: Pool's real 28s rank-1 cooldown added where the text said 'fifteen-second invitation'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabrications. (a) 'E dash charges' / 'E charges' appears three times — Quickdraw has no charges; it is one dash on 16/15/14/13/12s whose cooldown is lowered by landing basic attacks. (b) 'blind a key Transfusion-recovery auto with Smoke Screen' — W is not a blind; Riot's text is a cloud that reduces sight range, plus an impact slow. (c) "End of the Line's cone" appears twice — Q detonates after 1 second or on terrain; the cone belongs to Collateral Damage (R). The real interaction worth stating instead is that Sanguine Pool's 2 seconds of untargetability eats a committed R outright, which the page does say correctly in spikes[1].
audit.why: A player counting on a second dash charge commits with no exit into the one champion who can pool, wait it out and drain him back to full.
audit.corrected: Charges removed, W described as sight denial, Q described as a detonation.

audit.why: Anti-heal is already called out in itemization, which is the single most matchup-relevant item note against Transfusion and Hemoplague both healing him.

edits.before: Vlad is one of the worst level-1s in the game and you're not much better — one ability, no E charges yet — so the lane opens slow; deny his Transfusion last-hits and don't burn your dash chasing a single CS. The real prize is Levels 2-3: he has no escape and likely no W point yet, so E in, dump the point-blank 4-shell spread, and detonate End of the Line's cone on him. His E poke (Tides of Blood) is item-less AP right now and can't out-DPS your sustained short-range burst, so this 2-3 window is where you build your lead before Sanguine Pool is ever a factor.
edits.after: Vlad is one of the worst level-1s in the game and you're not much better — one ability, no Quickdraw yet — so the lane opens slow; deny his Transfusion last-hits and don't burn your dash chasing a single CS. The real prize is Levels 2-3: he has no escape and likely no W point yet, so E in, dump the point-blank 4-shell spread, and detonate End of the Line on him. Tides of Blood costs him his own health and is item-less AP right now, so this 2-3 window is where you build your lead before Sanguine Pool is ever a factor.

edits.before: Through Levels 4-5 you still out-trade a pre-Rylai Vlad if you can pin him in your shell range, but he'll start respecting your E dash and freeing up his Transfusion to heal back the poke. At 6 a W point and ult change everything — Sanguine Pool makes him untargetable, so a mistimed Collateral Damage whiffs entirely and his ult amps the AoE that punishes you for diving. Don't throw R into a healthy Vlad; bait the pool with a Q+auto first, and only commit your reload and R once it's down and on its long cooldown. Catching him mid-Transfusion before he can pool is your last clean kill setup.
edits.after: Through Levels 4-5 you still out-trade a pre-Rylai Vlad if you can pin him in your shell range, but he'll start respecting your E dash and freeing up his Transfusion to heal back the poke. At 6 a W point and ult change everything — Sanguine Pool is 2 seconds untargetable, so a mistimed Collateral Damage whiffs outright and Hemoplague amps everything that lands on you. Don't throw a 100-second R into a healthy Vlad; bait the pool with a Q or auto first, then commit your reload and R across its 28-second downtime. Catching him mid-Transfusion is your last clean kill setup.

notes: 35.71% over 42 games with an EVEN label was the biggest problem here — the page told the player to fight a lane he loses. diff itself was left as 'EVEN' rather than guessed at, because I could not confirm the accepted token set for that field from the brief; diffRating and both difficulty prose lines carry the correction instead. QUESTION for the user is recorded separately. The 'E charges' and 'Smoke Screen blinds' errors are Graves-wide boilerplate, not local to Vladimir.
